releases.notes:
# Family Tree 1.4.0

## Breeding planner

Pick two animals and Family Tree shows what their baby can be before you feed them. Choose **Breeding planner** at the top of the browser, or select an animal in the tree and choose **Plan breeding**. Shift-click a second card first to plan that pair.

- For horses, donkeys, mules, llamas, and trader llamas, each foal stat gets its lowest, most likely, and highest value, a bar showing how likely each value is, and the chance the foal beats both parents. Speed is in blocks per second, jump in blocks, and health in hearts. Llamas show chest slots first.
- The odds come from Minecraft's own breeding code, which is the same on every supported version from 1.20.1 to the 26.4 snapshot. A foal's stat lands around its parents' average, spread by the gap between the parents plus 30% of the stat's whole range, and a value past the game's limit bounces back inside it. Family Tree computes those chances exactly instead of sampling.
- A llama foal's strength is a random number from 1 up to the stronger parent's strength, with a 3% chance of one more. The weaker parent doesn't matter, and only that 3% roll can beat the stronger parent.
- Every camel has the same stats, so the planner says so instead of showing ranges.
- A horse and a donkey plan a mule. A llama and a trader llama can have either kind of foal, depending on which parent's breeding code runs.
- The planner warns when a parent is still a baby, or when it isn't loaded nearby and was born in the last two world days.
- The baby gets its species' word in each language: foal, lamb, calf, piglet, kitten, and so on, or a neutral word where a language has none.

Players without the client mod can plan too. `/familytree breed <a> <b>` prints the prediction and the relationship in chat, with the same name and UUID rules as the other commands. In the chest menu, a pet's family page has **Plan breeding**, which lists possible mates and opens the plan as a book. A wolf plan fits on two pages, with each stat's chance to beat both parents right under it. Both use only animals the player may view.

## Variant odds

The planner lists each possible variant with its chance:

- Sheep mix wool colors through the dye recipes, so red and white always make a pink lamb. Colors without a recipe give either parent's color.
- Axolotls take a parent's color, except 1 time in 1,200 when the baby is blue.
- Mooshrooms take a parent's color. Two parents of the same color have a 1 in 1,024 chance of the other color.
- Pandas pass one of each parent's two genes, and each gene can turn random 1 time in 32. The odds are grouped by how the cub looks and which hidden gene it carries.
- Horses keep a parent's coat 4 times in 9 each and get any coat 1 time in 9. Markings work the same way with 2 in 5 for each parent.
- Cats, wolves, llamas, foxes, and the warm and cold cows, pigs, and chickens of 1.21.5 and newer take either parent's variant, half the time each. The plan names both, such as "Variant: Pale 50%, Woods 50%" for two wolves.
- Rabbits take a parent's coat 19 times in 20. The rest of the time the biome where the baby is born picks the coat, and the planner shows that share as decided by the biome.

Frogs are left out, because a frog's color depends on the biome where its tadpole grows up. Animals from other mods are left out because Family Tree can't read their rules.

## How two animals are related

Shift-click a second card in the tree. The panel names the relationship in plain words, such as "Quill and Sorrel are half siblings" or "Aspen and Briar are first cousins", and the cards and links between them light up. Shift-click the card again to stop comparing. When the history has no shared ancestor, the panel says they are "not related as far as Family Tree knows".

releases.notes:
# Family Tree 1.3.0

## Chest menus for players without the client mod

Players who join a Family Tree server with an unmodded client can now type `/familytree` to browse in chest menus. Server admins no longer need every player to install the client mod.

- The pet list shows spawn egg icons, names, age, and living or deceased status, 45 pets to a page. Filter by status or species, or search by name in an anvil.
- Click a pet to see its parents, grandparents, and children, and click any relative to move through the family.
- Owners and operators can locate the pet in chat, rename it in Family Tree through an anvil, add or clear its parents with a picker and a confirmation step, and read the family as a written book on a lectern screen.
- The menus follow the screens' permissions and cooldowns. They never show coordinates, and other players' pets are view-only.
- Every click in a menu is refused before Minecraft moves an item. Shift-click, number keys, dragging, double-click, the offhand key, dropping, and closing with an item on the cursor leave the player's inventory unchanged.
- Players with the client mod keep the full screens. `/familytree` prints the command list and the key that opens them, and `/familytree menu` opens the chest menu.
- `vanillaMenu=false` in `config/familytree-server.properties` turns the menu off. `commandAliases=pets,ft` adds other names for `/familytree`.

The family tree is not drawn on a map item. Text on a 128-pixel map needs a server-side bitmap font, which would leave pet names in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and other scripts unreadable, and each map adds a permanent file to the world.

## Translations

Family Tree now includes Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Ukrainian, German, French, Italian, Spanish for Spain and for Mexico, Brazilian Portuguese, Polish, and Turkish. The translations are machine-made, and corrections are welcome on GitHub.

- The server also answers in these languages. Chat messages from commands and the linking stick, and all chest menu text, use the player's Minecraft language when a translation exists, and English otherwise. This works for players without the client mod too.
- Species names in the browser, picker, chat, and menus now come from Minecraft's own entity names, so they follow the game language. `/familytree list` and `/familytree info` no longer contain fixed English text.
- A unit test checks that every language file has exactly the keys and format arguments of the English file.

## Every animal you breed

Family Tree now records cows, mooshrooms, sheep, pigs, chickens, rabbits, goats, foxes, axolotls, frogs, bees, turtles, pandas, ocelots, hoglins, striders, sniffers, armadillos, and breedable animals from other mods, next to your pets.

- Wild animals stay out of the history until a player breeds them, uses a name tag on one, or clicks one with the linking stick. Breeding records the baby and both parents. The player who fed, named, or added them owns them in Family Tree, and babies of a recorded family stay with that family's owner.
- Families already in the history keep growing when their animals breed without a player.
- Frogs, sniffers, and turtles hatch from spawn or eggs, so Minecraft never links their babies to the parents. Breeding frogs or sniffers still adds both parents for the player; turtles need a name tag or the linking stick. Name or add the hatchlings, then use **Add parents**.
- Unnamed animals other than pets get their species and a short code as a name, such as "Sheep 3F2A1C". The name comes from the species id, so it stays the same when you change languages. The pet names stay free for pets.
- `/familytree info` and the linking stick work for every recorded animal. `/familytree list` stops after 100 lines on large farms.

## Variants and rare outcomes

releases.notes:
# Family Tree 1.2.0

## Horse breeding stats

Family Tree records speed, jump height, and health for horses, donkeys, mules, llamas, trader llamas, camels, skeleton horses, and zombie horses. Speed is in blocks per second, jump in blocks, and health in hearts, using the Minecraft Wiki's conversions. Llamas also show strength and their chest slots.

- Tree cards show each animal's stats. A green ▲ marks a stat higher than both parents, and a red ▼ marks one lower than both.
- Select a pet in the tree to compare each stat with both parents' values. Small windows and large GUI scales show a one-line summary instead.
- **Sort** in the browser orders pets by speed, jump, or health. Pets without stats follow in name order.
- Exported PNGs include the stats and a legend for the markers.
- Settings has **Show horse stats** to hide the stats everywhere, including exports.
- `/familytree info <name>` lists the stats.
- Horses, donkeys, mules, skeleton horses, and zombie horses have portraits. In the game they match coat and markings; exports show a side profile cut from the animal's texture. Llamas and camels have in-game portraits only.

Stats are base values, so potion effects don't change them. Family Tree reads them when it records an animal and again whenever the server loads, unloads, or scans it.

## Camels and skeleton trap horses

Minecraft treats every camel as tamed, and skeleton trap horses are tamed without an owner. Version 1.1.0 recorded each of these animals as soon as it loaded, without an owner, so only operators could see them. Now Family Tree records them once a player rides or breeds them, and that player becomes their owner in Family Tree. Minecraft's own ownership stays unchanged. Wild camels nobody rides stay out of the tree. Ownerless records that 1.1.0 already saved stay in the history, and the first player to ride one of those animals becomes its owner.

Foals that are not tamed yet keep their last known location and stats current, because their record already exists from breeding.

## Minecraft 1.21.11

Family Tree now has Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 1.21.11. Fabric needs Fabric API for 1.21.11. NeoForge needs 21.11.48 or newer within 21.11. Both builds run on Java 21.

- A 1.21.1 world upgraded to 1.21.11 keeps its Family Tree history. Both versions save to the same file, so nothing gets imported or converted. When the world later moves to 26.x, Family Tree imports that file once, as it does for 1.21.1 worlds.
- Tamed nautiluses and zombie nautiluses are recorded, and foals from bred nautiluses keep their parents. They have no portraits; the browser shows the first letter of the name.

## Minecraft 1.20.1 on Fabric and Forge

Family Tree now runs on Minecraft 1.20.1. The Fabric build needs Fabric API 0.92.x for 1.20.1, and the Forge build needs Forge 47.1.0 or newer. Both run on Java 17 and include horse stats and every other feature of the newer builds.

- 1.20.1 worlds keep their history in `data/familytree.dat`, the same file and format that 1.21.1 uses. A 1.20.1 world upgraded to 1.21.1 kept its pets, parents, and deaths in testing.
- Wolves in 1.20.1 have a single coat, so wolf portraits use the tamed wolf texture. Cat and horse portraits match their coats.
- Forge uses the same channel names as the other builds and registers protocol 3. Players without Family Tree can join a Forge server that runs it.

## Quilt

The Fabric builds are now listed for Quilt. With Quilt Loader 0.30.1 and Fabric API, a dedicated server started with Family Tree on all seven Fabric targets. Clients on 1.21.1 and 26.3 joined a Quilt server, received the welcome message, and opened the browser. Older Quilt Loader releases such as 0.24 report a Fabric Loader version below Family Tree's minimum, so Quilt refuses to start the mod on them.

## Upgrade

Update the server and clients together. This release changes the snapshot, open, discovery, and rename channels, and NeoForge registers protocol 3.

releases.notes:
# Family Tree 1.1.0

Add known parents without commands. Select a pet in the tree, choose Add parents, search for both parents, and confirm. Clear recorded parents through a confirmation screen. Horse and donkey parents can link to a mule.

The browser has Getting started and Refresh. The tree also has Refresh and Open folder after export. Export reports the actual PNG filename. The selected browser filter is visible.

## Supported builds

Fabric supports Minecraft 1.21.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2, 26.2, and 26.3. It requires Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer and the matching Fabric API. NeoForge supports 1.21.1 with 21.1.252, 26.2 with 26.2.0.88, and 26.3 with 26.3.0.37-beta. The NeoForge 26.3 release is beta because its loader is beta. Minecraft 1.21.1 uses Java 21; the 26.x builds use Java 25.

## Reliability

- Family snapshots use pages below 256 KiB. The browser shows a completed snapshot and rejects incomplete replies. Tests cover a 10,000-pet snapshot with Unicode names. Snapshots above 100,000 visible records fail with a message rather than silently omitting pets.
- Commands and network requests share cooldowns for loaded-pet scans. Open, rename, locate, and parent-edit requests also have cooldowns.
- Generation calculation uses an explicit stack and passes a 10,000-generation test.
- Unreadable and duplicate save entries remain in the next save. Unsupported future save formats disable edits and preserve the original data. Check the server log for recovery details.
- Legacy import runs once for a new store and copies the old file to a migration backup. Empty modern stores do not import old history again.
- Name-based edits reject ambiguous matches. Use one of the UUIDs printed in chat. Locate still reports all permitted name matches and also accepts an exact UUID.
- Operator pruning writes a JSON backup under the world's `familytree-backups/` directory. A failed backup cancels deletion.
- Jars use exact Minecraft version predicates and include the MIT license, icon, and source links. Linking sessions and portrait caches clear on disconnect.

## Upgrade

Update the server and clients together. This release changes snapshot, open-request, discovery, and NeoForge protocol identifiers. Existing saved record field names stay unchanged.

Back up the world before upgrading. Older mod releases can drop fields they do not understand when saving, and older releases do not protect future formats. Minecraft world downgrades remain unsupported.

A focused tree displays up to six generations in either direction. Use a species view for all its families. Screens refresh when requested rather than updating automatically while open. Revival mods, altered pet models, and modded species still need separate compatibility testing.

## Family Tree 0.3.1

Small quality-of-life update.

### Default keybind
The **Open Family Tree** key is now bound to **H** by default (previously unbound). You can still rebind it under **Options > Controls > Family Tree**. If you already changed or saved this binding before, your existing setting is kept.

### Compatibility
- Fully save-compatible with 0.3.0 and earlier worlds.
- Minecraft 26.1.1, Fabric Loader >= 0.16, Fabric API, Java 25.

releases.notes:
## Family Tree 0.3.0

Three quality-of-life features for keeping track of your pets:

### Pet locator
`/familytree locate <name>` shows a pet's coordinates, dimension, and distance from you. If the pet's chunk is unloaded you get its last known position with a "last seen day N" note. If several pets share the name, all of them are listed. Operators get clickable coordinates that pre-fill a teleport command.

### Death cause
When a tracked pet dies, the mod now records what killed it. Tree nodes show "Slain by Creeper, day 43" or "Died of fall, day 12" instead of just "deceased". `/familytree list` shows it too.

### Linking stick glow
Pets clicked with the `familytree` stick now glow for about 5 seconds, so you can tell which cat in a pile you actually selected.

### Compatibility
- Fully save-compatible: existing worlds load unchanged, old records just have no location/death cause yet.
- Run `/familytree scan` (or wait for pets to be seen) to populate locations for existing pets.
- Minecraft 26.1.1, Fabric Loader >= 0.16, Fabric API, Java 25.

## Family Tree 0.2.0

For Minecraft 26.1.1 · Fabric Loader 0.19.2+ · Fabric API · Java 25

### New: Linking stick 🪄

Made for existing worlds where your pets were tamed or bred before installing the mod:

- Rename a plain **stick** to `familytree` in an anvil (case-insensitive) to turn it into the linking tool.
- Right-click **parent 1 → parent 2 → child**, then confirm with clickable **[Confirm]** / **[Cancel]** chat buttons to record the parentage.
- **Sneak + right-click** a pet to clear its recorded parents (with confirmation).
- Every click shows the pet's currently-known parents and children, creates a tracker record on the spot if the pet has none, and picks up nametag names.
- Only tamed pets of the same species can be linked; pets don't sit down while you're using the tool.

### Improvements

- **Family tree layout fix**: children are now always placed below both parents, and mates (e.g. an outside pet that had kittens with one of your tracked cats) are placed side by side on the same row.
- "Show age" and "Show birth day" display settings now default to **off**.

### Install

Drop `familytree-0.2.0.jar` into your `mods` folder on the server (or singleplayer instance); install on the client too to use the in-game screen.
